# AarogyaSeva — Rural Healthcare Intelligence Mesh
### AIRAVAT 3.0 · Hackathon Edition

> **Offline-first, AI-powered clinical decision support for Community Health Workers (CHWs) in rural India.**
> Runs entirely on-device — no cloud dependency, no internet required.

## 1. Project Overview

AarogyaSeva is a clinical intelligence platform built for Community Health Workers (CHWs) operating in rural India — areas with unreliable connectivity, low-spec devices, and high patient loads. The system:

- **Runs fully offline** — all ML inference is on-device (ONNX, TFLite, scikit-learn)
- **Coordinates across CHW devices** via a P2P gossip mesh (no central server required)
- **Provides explainable AI predictions** — every ML output includes plain-language reasoning, confidence bands, and SHAP-derived feature signals
- **Supports 5 clinical domains** — hemorrhage, TB adherence, pesticide poisoning, diabetic foot ulcers, surgical site infections
- **Speaks local languages** — voice transcription + translation for Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali

The CHW interacts through a modern web UI (installable as a PWA) that is patient-centric, navigation-first, and designed for low-literacy, high-stress use.

## 2. Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    FRONTEND (Next.js PWA)                │
│  /dashboard → /patient/[id] → /patient/[id]/agents       │
│  React 19 · Tailwind CSS v4 · Zustand · Three.js         │
└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                     │ HTTP REST (localhost:8000/api/v1)
                     │ Offline fallback: mockData.ts
                     ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               BACKEND (FastAPI + Python 3.13)            │
│                                                          │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐               │
│  │ Pillar 1 │  │ Pillar 2 │  │ Pillar 3 │  ...          │
│  │  PPH     │  │    TB    │  │ Pesticide│               │
│  └──────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘               │
│                                                          │
│  EventBus (pub/sub) · Explainability · FL Training       │
│                                                          │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │         SQLite (mesh.db) via SQLAlchemy Async     │   │
│  │   WAL mode · FK enforcement · 64MB page cache     │   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                     │
          ◄──────────┴──────────►
     P2P Gossip Mesh (BLE / WiFi-Direct / 2G)
     CHW Device ↔ CHW Device (CRDT sync)
```

## 3. Tech Stack

### Backend
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Web Framework | FastAPI 0.111+ |
| Language | Python 3.13 |
| Database | SQLite (`mesh.db`) via SQLAlchemy 2.0 async + aiosqlite |
| Migrations | Alembic |
| ML Inference | ONNX Runtime 1.20+, scikit-learn, joblib |
| Image Inference | ONNX Runtime (converted from TFLite via tf2onnx) |
| Explainability | SHAP (tabular), GradCAM (image) |
| LLM | Gemma-4 E2B Instruct Q4_K_M via llama-cpp-python (on-device) |
| Voice / ASR | Vosk (offline), Whisper (tiny) |
| Translation | AI4Bharat IndicTrans2 (Indic ↔ English) |
| Synthetic Data | CTGAN (SDV) |
| Federated Learning | Gossip-based FedAvg (no central server) |
| Task Queue | APScheduler (background sync jobs) |
| Package Manager | uv |

### Frontend
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Framework | Next.js 16.2 (App Router) |
| Language | TypeScript 5, React 19 |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 |
| State | Zustand 5 |
| 3D Graphics | Three.js + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei |
| Animation | Framer Motion |
| Icons | Lucide React |
| Offline DB | Dexie (IndexedDB wrapper) |
| PWA | @ducanh2912/next-pwa |

## 5. Backend — Setup & Run

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.11+ (project targets 3.13; 3.11 also works)
- [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) package manager

### Install dependencies

```bash
cd AarogyaSeva/backend

# Option A: using uv (recommended)
uv pip install -r requirements.txt --python .venv/bin/python

# Option B: using pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Initialise & seed the database

This creates `mesh.db` with all 17 tables and populates it with 10 realistic mock patients, 6 active clinical alerts, and 30 days of TB dose logs:

```bash
# From the backend directory
.venv/bin/python seed_db.py
```

The script is **fully idempotent** — safe to re-run, skips existing records.

Expected output:
```
[1/4] Initialising database schema (all 17 tables)...  ✓ Schema ready
[2/4] Seeding patients (10 records)...                 ✓ 10 patient(s) inserted
[3/4] Seeding active alerts (6 records)...             ✓ 6 alert(s) inserted
[4/4] Seeding TB dose logs (30 days × 2 patients)...   ✓ 60 dose log(s) inserted
```

### Run the server

```bash
uvicorn main:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

The API will be available at:
- **Base URL**: `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`
- **Swagger UI**: `http://localhost:8000/docs`
- **Health Check**: `http://localhost:8000/health`

## 6. Frontend — Setup & Run

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- npm or pnpm

### Install & run

```bash
cd AarogyaSeva/frontend/my-app

npm install
npm run dev
```

The app will be available at `http://localhost:3000`.

### Environment Variables (optional)

Create `frontend/my-app/.env.local` to override the API base URL:

```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/v1
```

If not set, defaults to `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`.

> **Offline mode**: If the backend is unreachable, the frontend automatically falls back to `src/lib/mockData.ts` — the UI remains fully functional with mock patients.

### Build for production

```bash
npm run build
npm run start
```

## 7. Database

The database is a **single SQLite file** (`backend/mesh.db`) managed by SQLAlchemy async ORM with aiosqlite.

### SQLite Configuration (set on every connection)
| Pragma | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `journal_mode` | WAL | Concurrent readers + one writer |
| `foreign_keys` | ON | FK constraint enforcement |
| `synchronous` | NORMAL | Durability vs. write speed balance |
| `cache_size` | -65536 (64MB) | Reduced disk I/O on slow storage |
| `busy_timeout` | 5000ms | Prevent "database is locked" errors |

### Tables (17 total)

| Pillar | Table(s) |
|---|---|
| P1 PPH | `pph_assessments` |
| P2 TB | `dose_logs`, `adherence_records` |
| P3 Pesticide | `pesticide_assessments` |
| P4 DFU | `dfu_assessments`, `wound_images` |
| P5 SSI | `ssi_assessments`, `postop_records` |
| P6 Voice | `transcription_logs` |
| P7 CHW | `patients`, `alerts`, `checklist_completions`, `sync_logs` |
| P8 Explainability | `explanation_audit_log` |
| P9 Synthetic | `synthetic_data_jobs`, `fl_rounds`, `model_versions` |

### Seeded Mock Data

| Table | Records |
|---|---|
| `patients` | 10 (p-001 → p-010, all under `CHW-7834-IND`) |
| `alerts` | 6 active unresolved (3 critical, 3 medium) |
| `dose_logs` | 60 (30 days × 2 TB patients: Ramesh Kumar, Mohan Lal) |
| `adherence_records` | 2 (one per TB patient, 28/30 compliance, 2 consecutive misses) |

## 8. API Reference

Base URL: `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`

All ML endpoints return a standard **`ExplainedOutput`** envelope:

```json

  "probability": 0.82,
  "confidence_band": "HIGH",
  "top_signals": [
    { "feature": "systolic_bp", "weight": 0.41, "direction": "increases_risk" }

  "plain_language_explanation": "Blood pressure consistently above 140/90...",
  "recommended_action": "Immediate obstetric evaluation required.",

```

## 9. ML Pillars (9 Agents)

### P1 — Postpartum Hemorrhage (ONNX)
Scores hemorrhage risk from: systolic/diastolic BP, pulse, blood loss (mL), uterine tone, pallor, parity, gestational age, PPH history. Missing values are mean-imputed and flagged. Output: `LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH` with SHAP-derived signals.

### P2 — TB DOTS Adherence (ONNX + Rule Engine)
Tracks daily dose intake. Computes 7-day and 30-day adherence windows. Scores relapse risk based on consecutive misses, adherence %, and symptom flags. Integrates with the EventBus to auto-alert CHW on 2+ consecutive misses.

### P3 — Pesticide Poisoning (scikit-learn / joblib)
Classifies toxidrome type (organophosphate, carbamate, pyrethroid, unknown) from 8 cholinergic symptom flags + occupational context. Provides severity triage (MILD/MODERATE/SEVERE) and first-response action list.

### P4 — Diabetic Foot Ulcer (TFLite → ONNX)
Accepts wound photograph, runs image quality gate (blur/brightness), then classifies Wagner grade (0–5) and detects active infection. Tracks progression across visits. GradCAM heatmap shows which wound regions drove the prediction.

### P5 — Surgical Site Infection (CDC Rule Engine)
CDC-criteria SSI classification (superficial / deep / organ space / no_ssi) from days post-op, temperature, and 8 clinical sign checkboxes. Calibrated probability with confidence bands.

### P6 — Voice NLU
Multi-stage pipeline: Vosk/Whisper ASR → IndicTrans2 translation → intent/entity extraction → EventBus routing. Supports 8 Indic languages. Enables voice-driven DOTS logging, patient lookup, and CHW queries.

### P7 — CHW Companion
Master patient registry. Aggregates real-time risk scores from all other agents per patient. Provides prioritised dashboard, condition-specific clinical checklists, on-device LLM (Gemma-4 E2B) answers, and CRDT-based P2P sync.

### P8 — Explainability & Audit
Every `ExplainedOutput` from every agent is persisted in `explanation_audit_log`. Provides plain-language explanations, SHAP feature attribution, confidence bands, and GradCAM heatmaps. Audit trail is the primary training signal for federated learning.

### P9 — Synthetic Data & Federated Learning
CTGAN-based synthetic patient data generation for model training on low-data conditions. Gossip-based FedAvg federated learning: CHW devices exchange model weight deltas over P2P mesh without sharing raw patient data.

## 10. Frontend Pages & Components

### Pages

| Route | Description |
|---|---|
| `/dashboard` | CHW home screen — KPI cards, live patient registry, alert feed, AI pillar status, mesh node map |
| `/patient/[id]` | Patient detail — large serif header, vitals grid, ML prediction cards, clinical timeline, care plan |
| `/patient/[id]/agents` | **Agent Mesh** — 5 AI agent cards; clicking any card reveals a full input form for that agent, submits to backend, displays `ExplanationCard` result |

### Key Components

**`DashboardLayout`** — Persistent sidebar with route-aware navigation. The "Agent Mesh" link is patient-scoped: when inside a patient page, it links to `/patient/[id]/agents`; from the dashboard, it links to the mesh overview.

**`ExplanationCard`** — Reusable component for rendering any `ExplainedOutput`:
- Colour-coded confidence bands (HIGH=rose, MEDIUM=amber, LOW=stone)
- Animated progress bar
- Pulsing escalation badge for critical predictions
- Expandable SHAP signals panel with feature weights and directions
- Missing data and limitations disclosure

**`StethoscopeBackdrop`** — Three.js 3D rotating stethoscope rendered inline in the dashboard hero section using `@react-three/fiber`. Dynamically imported with `ssr: false`.

**`NewPatientModal`** — Form modal for adding patients directly from the dashboard. New patients are optimistically added to local state.

### Agent Mesh Input Forms

Each of the 5 agents has a purpose-built form:

| Agent | Key Inputs |
|---|---|
| PPH | Systolic/diastolic BP, pulse, blood loss mL, parity, gestational age, uterine tone, pallor, history |
| TB | One-click (pulls 30-day dose history from DB automatically) |
| Pesticide | 8 cholinergic symptom toggles, crop season, chemical class |
| DFU | Image file upload with preview (uses device camera on mobile) |
| SSI | Days post-op, temperature, 8 clinical sign checkboxes |

## 11. Design System

The frontend follows the **"Digital Hearth"** design philosophy — a clinical-grade editorial aesthetic emphasising trust, clarity, and warmth.

### Typography
- **Headlines**: Newsreader (serif) — signals trust, medical authority
- **Body / UI**: Inter (sans-serif) — legibility at small sizes

### Colour Tokens
| Token | Use |
|---|---|
| `surface` / `background` | Warm off-white (`#f8f8f4`) |
| `primary` | Deep teal-charcoal (`#2d3435`) |
| `secondary` | Muted slate (`#5e5e5e`) |
| Accent green | `emerald-*` for healthy/stable states |
| Accent red | `rose-*` / `red-*` for critical/high risk |
| Accent amber | `amber-*` for medium risk / warnings |

### Key Design Rules
- **No divider lines** — boundaries created by tonal background shifts and negative space
- **Glass & gradient CTAs** — primary actions use `bg-gradient-to-r` with `backdrop-blur`
- **Tonal layering** — elevation expressed via background colour depth, not shadows
- **Asymmetric layouts** — intentional imbalance creates editorial rhythm
- **Intelligence Mesh gradient** — `from-emerald-50 via-teal-50 to-stone-100` used in hero and agent sections
